content.title: Fuel Cells
content.description: A fuel cell is an electrochemical device that converts the chemical energy of a fuel directly into electrical energy through redox reactions. Unlike batteries, fuel cells continuously generate electricity as long as fuel and oxidant are supplied.

content.content: Fuel cells are clean and efficient energy sources used in transportation, portable power systems, and stationary power generation. Common fuel cells include Methanol-Oxygen Fuel Cells and Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFC).

content.title: Why Fuel Cells?
content.content: Fuel cells provide high efficiency, continuous power generation, low pollution, and reduced dependence on fossil fuels.

The Methanol-Oxygen Fuel Cell uses methanol as fuel and oxygen from air as the oxidant. It consists of an anode, cathode, electrolyte, and catalyst. Methanol is oxidized at the anode while oxygen is reduced at the cathode, producing electricity, water, and carbon dioxide.

A Solid Oxide Fuel Cell uses a solid ceramic electrolyte that conducts oxide ions at high temperatures. It commonly uses hydrogen or natural gas as fuel and oxygen as the oxidant, providing high electrical efficiency.

items.question: Methanol-Oxygen Fuel Cell
items.answer: Used in portable electronics, backup power systems, and small electric vehicles.

items.question: Solid Oxide Fuel Cell
items.answer: Used in power plants, industries, and distributed electricity generation.

items.question: Transportation
items.answer: Fuel cells are used in buses, cars, and hydrogen-powered vehicles.

items.question: Environmental Benefit
items.answer: Fuel cells produce lower emissions and higher efficiency than conventional power sources.

content.title: Key Advantage
content.content: Fuel cells can generate electricity continuously as long as fuel is supplied, making them suitable for long-duration power applications.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Fuel cells convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy.
Fuel cells require continuous fuel supply.
Methanol-Oxygen fuel cells use methanol as fuel.
SOFC uses a solid ceramic electrolyte and operates at high temperature.
Fuel cells are efficient, clean, and suitable for continuous power generation.
